past_medical_history: Essential hypertension for 35 years, historically poorly controlled
Chronic kidney disease stage 3b (eGFR 38), attributed to hypertensive nephrosclerosis
Left ventricular hypertrophy on a previous echocardiogram
family_history: Father died suddenly at 62, presumed stroke
Mother had hypertension and heart failure
Two brothers with hypertension, one on dialysis

social_history.living_situation: Lives with his son's family; his daughter-in-law manages his medication

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented to person and place, year correct, date incorrect by four days. MoCA 21/30 with losses in trail-making, clock, digit span backwards, fluency (10 animals) and delayed recall (3/5 unaided, 5/5 cued). Answers are correct but slow.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full. Fundi show grade 2 hypertensive retinopathy with arteriolar narrowing and arteriovenous nipping. Visual fields full. Face symmetric. Speech mildly dysarthric.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk. Tone increased in both legs. Strength 5/5 with 4+/5 hip flexion bilaterally.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 3+ knees, 2+ ankles, plantar responses extensor bilaterally. Palmomental present.
neurological_exam.coordination: Intact in the upper limbs; mild bilateral heel-to-shin clumsiness.
neurological_exam.gait: Markedly short-stepped, wide-based, low clearance, with preserved arm swing. Requires the chair arms to rise. Turns in six steps. Three falls in the past year. Tandem impossible.
neurological_exam.additional: Frontal release signs present. Urinary frequency and urgency, partly attributed to prostatism. No tremor, no rigidity.

patient.chief_complaint: Falls and progressive slowing over two years, with the family reporting he can no longer be left alone
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Samuel Adeyemi is a 78-year-old retired bus driver who lives with his son and attends with his daughter-in-law. Over two years he has become progressively slower in thought and in movement, and over the past year he has fallen three times, always while turning or rising. The family's chief concern is safety: he leaves the tap running, cannot manage his own medication, and last month took a bus in the wrong direction and had to be collected. His memory for recent events is patchy but improves markedly when he is reminded of the setting; his daughter-in-law says he 'knows it when you tell him where it happened'. He has no discrete episodes of weakness or speech loss that the family can date. He has had hypertension for thirty-five years, was lost to follow-up for a long period in his fifties, and now has stage 3b chronic kidney disease and left ventricular hypertrophy attributed to it. His blood pressure at this visit is 176/96 despite three agents. There are no hallucinations, no fluctuation across the day, no dream enactment and no rest tremor. Urinary urgency is present and has been attributed to his prostate.

findings.type: White matter hyperintensity of presumed vascular origin
findings.location: Confluent periventricular and deep white matter throughout both hemispheres

signal_characteristics.T2_FLAIR: Extensive confluent hyperintensity involving the external capsules and pontine tegmentum

findings.location: Bilateral thalami, right putamen, left caudate, pons, bilateral corona radiata

signal_characteristics.T2: Numerous CSF-signal spaces in the inferior basal ganglia

signal_characteristics.SWI: Rounded foci of signal loss in a strictly deep distribution; no lobar microbleed and no cortical superficial siderosis

findings.location: Global with preserved medial temporal lobes

volumetrics.ventricular_system: Evans index 0.30, proportionate to volume loss

additional_observations: Severe small-vessel burden with a strictly deep microbleed distribution, indicating hypertensive arteriopathy
No lobar microbleeds and no cortical superficial siderosis — the Boston criteria for amyloid angiopathy are not met
No cortical infarct in any arterial territory
No hydrocephalus, no mass, no abnormal enhancement
mri.impression: Very severe sporadic hypertensive small-vessel disease: Fazekas 3 confluent white matter change, eight chronic lacunes, severe basal-ganglia perivascular space enlargement and four strictly deep microbleeds. Medial temporal lobes preserved. The burden accounts for both the cognitive syndrome and the gait disorder.

labs.interpretation: Creatinine 1.92 mg/dL with eGFR 38 confirms stage 3b chronic kidney disease. Normocytic anaemia at 11.8 g/dL is consistent with renal disease. LDL 96 mg/dL is near but not at the secondary-prevention target. TSH, B12, folate, RPR and HIV are normal or negative, excluding reversible causes.

specialized_test.impression: With education-adjusted norms the profile remains clearly subcortical: severe executive and processing-speed impairment with preserved recognition memory and naming. Low education does not account for the deficit.

findings.performance: Trail-making 0/1, clock planning impaired, fluency 10 — impaired

clinical_assessment.impression: MoCA 21/30 in a patient with ten years of formal education, with the deficit concentrated in executive function, attention and processing speed and recall fully responsive to cueing. Functional independence is lost. The profile is subcortical.

findings.result: Slow, requires arm support to rise
Three falls in 12 months, all on turning or rising

output.impression: Timed-up-and-go 24.6 s with a short-stepped, wide-based, low-clearance gait, preserved arm swing and an inability to rise without arm support. This is a high falls risk and part of the subcortical vascular syndrome rather than an incidental orthopaedic problem.

background.posterior_dominant_rhythm: 9 Hz, symmetric, reactive to eye opening

eeg.impression: Normal awake EEG for age. No epileptiform discharges and no focal or generalised slowing.

labs.interpretation: The additional panels requested are negative and do not contribute to the diagnosis in this presentation.

findings.signal: study performed and reported as non-contributory
findings.description: no finding relevant to this presentation

advanced_imaging.impression: The study was performed and does not contribute to the diagnosis in this presentation.

additional_observations: Chronic ischaemic white matter change, better characterised on the MRI already obtained
ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No haemorrhage, mass or hydrocephalus. CT cannot exclude microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis.

findings: No intracardiac thrombus, vegetation or shunt. No pericardial effusion.
No atrial fibrillation. No pauses. No AV block.

vascular_cognitive_impairment.query: vascular cognitive impairment diagnostic criteria and secondary prevention

results.title: Diagnostic criteria for vascular cognitive disorders: a VASCOG statement
results.authors: Sachdev P, Kalaria R, O'Brien J, et al.
results.summary: Requires a cognitive syndrome documented on a validated instrument plus imaging or temporal evidence that cerebrovascular disease accounts for it.

results.title: Neuroimaging standards for research into small vessel disease (STRIVE-2)
results.authors: Duering M, Biessels GJ, Brodtmann A, et al.
results.summary: Defines and standardises the reporting of white matter hyperintensity, lacunes, microbleeds, perivascular spaces and cortical superficial siderosis.

vascular_cognitive_impairment.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for vascular cognitive impairment; management is control of the vascular risk factors, secondary prevention matched to the mechanism, review of the anticholinergic burden, and treatment of coexisting Alzheimer pathology where biomarkers support it.

medication_review.proposed: review of the current medication list for anticholinergic burden
warnings: Anticholinergic load is a reversible contributor to cognitive impairment in this population and should be quantified before any new prescription.
medication_review.summary: No prohibitive interaction identified within the current list.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Vascular dementia — subcortical ischaemic (small-vessel) type, severe hypertensive arteriopathy with gait failure

differential.key_features: Gait failure with urinary urgency and cognitive impairment is the NPH triad, but the Evans index is 0.30 with ventriculomegaly proportionate to atrophy, there is no disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid space, and the gait is short-stepped rather than magnetic; the Fazekas 3 burden with eight lacunes explains the syndrome without invoking hydrocephalus
Cue-responsive recall, preserved medial temporal lobes and gait failure early in the course are all against it

Lower-body predominant gait disorder from the same small-vessel burden is a reasonable label for the motor syndrome, but there is no rest tremor, no rigidity and no levodopa responsiveness to establish
Stage 3b disease is a genuine contributor and shares the same hypertensive cause, but does not account for eight lacunes and a Fazekas 3 burden
No fluctuation, hallucinations, parkinsonism or dream enactment

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a collateral history from an informant who sees the patient daily: the shape of the decline (abrupt, stepwise or gradual), whether any step can be dated to a cerebrovascular event, and which instrumental activities have been lost
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Two years of progressive psychomotor slowing with early gait failure and three falls, cue-responsive memory complaints, loss of instrumental independence, and a 35-year history of poorly controlled hypertension with end-organ damage in the kidney, heart and retina

optimal_actions.action: Perform a validated bedside cognitive assessment and record the per-domain profile and whether delayed recall improves with cueing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: MoCA 21/30 with executive and processing-speed predominance, cue-responsive recall and lost instrumental independence

optimal_actions.action: Order the reversible-cause screen and the vascular-risk assays that will be treated (CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, RPR, HIV, HbA1c, lipid panel)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Reversible causes excluded; stage 3b chronic kidney disease with renal anaemia confirms hypertensive end-organ damage in a third organ

optimal_actions.action: Perform timed gait and balance testing: the short-stepped, wide-based gait with preserved arm swing is part of the subcortical syndrome and separates it from the gait of normal pressure hydrocephalus and of parkinsonian disorders
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Timed-up-and-go 24.6 s with severe short-stepped wide-based gait, inability to rise unaided, and a documented high falls risk

optimal_actions.action: Obtain brain MRI reported in STRIVE-2 terms — FLAIR for white matter hyperintensity with a Fazekas grade, T1/T2 for lacunes, DWI to establish that the lesions are chronic, and SWI for microbleeds and cortical superficial siderosis — together with the medial temporal atrophy grade
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Very severe small-vessel burden — Fazekas 3, eight lacunes, severe perivascular space enlargement, four strictly deep microbleeds — with preserved medial temporal lobes

optimal_actions.action: Order formal multi-domain neuropsychological testing to settle the executive-versus-amnestic attribution and to document a baseline for follow-up
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Subcortical profile confirmed with education-adjusted norms; recognition memory preserved

optimal_actions.action: Confirm the diagnostic criteria applied and the current secondary-prevention targets against the guidelines
optimal_actions.expected_finding: VASCOG 2014 criteria and the 2021 AHA/ASA secondary prevention targets confirmed

optimal_actions.action: Review the medication list for anticholinergic burden and for the interaction between antithrombotic choice and the microbleed burden before prescribing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Anticholinergic contributors identified and the antithrombotic choice reconciled with the imaging burden

optimal_actions.action: Intensify antihypertensive therapy cautiously toward a systolic target below 130 mmHg with renal monitoring, increase the statin to reach an LDL below 70 mg/dL, refer for falls-prevention physiotherapy and a home hazard assessment, and review the tamsulosin and the diuretic for orthostatic contribution
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Blood pressure lowered with renal function monitored, falls risk actively managed, and drugs contributing to orthostatic hypotension reviewed

optimal_actions.action: Disclose the diagnosis and its mechanism to the patient and the informant, and address driving, medication management, finances, advance care planning and caregiver support
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Patient and informant engaged in care planning; safety domains addressed

useless_tools.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role in vascular cognitive impairment; it belongs to the differential of a rapidly progressive or fluctuating course (Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, non-convulsive status, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy), none of which is present here

A presynaptic dopaminergic study answers the Lewy-body question, not the vascular one, and there is no spontaneous parkinsonism, no fluctuating cognition with hallucinations and no REM sleep behaviour disorder
Cardiac sympathetic imaging is a test for dementia with Lewy bodies and for autonomic failure; it says nothing about cerebrovascular disease

An untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune-encephalitis battery in a chronic stepwise decline with a hypertensive imaging burden is the archetypal expensive miss; the indication for those assays is a subacute multidomain syndrome
The MRI already obtained answers everything a CT could and more: CT cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis, so it cannot grade the vascular burden this diagnosis rests on
There is no embolic lesion pattern to explain: the burden here is small-vessel, and a structural cardioembolic source would not account for it
Prolonged rhythm monitoring is for an unexplained embolic infarct pattern; in pure small-vessel disease it changes nothing about the diagnosis or the treatment

sequence_constraints.reason: Document the cognitive deficit before attributing it: imaging read without a cognitive profile invites over-attribution of incidental white matter change

critical_actions: Document the cognitive deficit with education-adjusted instruments
Exclude reversible causes with the named screen and interpret them alongside the renal impairment
Obtain brain MRI with SWI and grade the burden in STRIVE-2 terms
Measure gait objectively and act on a timed-up-and-go of 24.6 s as a falls emergency
Distinguish this syndrome from normal pressure hydrocephalus on the ventricular measurements and the gait pattern before considering a tap test
Lower blood pressure toward target while monitoring renal function
Address home safety, medication supervision and caregiver support
contraindicated_actions: Do not proceed to a shunt evaluation on the strength of the clinical triad alone when the imaging shows ex vacuo ventriculomegaly and a severe small-vessel burden
Do not add anticoagulation: there is no cardioembolic indication and four deep microbleeds raise haemorrhagic risk
Do not prescribe anticholinergic bladder agents for the urinary urgency
Do not drop blood pressure precipitously in severe small-vessel disease; titrate with renal monitoring
Do not attribute the falls to age or to arthritis without measuring gait
key_reasoning_points: The NPH triad and severe small-vessel disease overlap almost completely in their clinical presentation; the discrimination is made on ventricular morphology, the disproportion of the subarachnoid spaces and the character of the gait, not on the triad itself
Hypertensive end-organ damage in the kidney, heart and retina corroborates the vascular attribution in a patient with no dateable stroke
A strictly deep microbleed distribution indicates hypertensive arteriopathy and, unlike a lobar distribution, does not by itself prohibit antithrombotic therapy
A timed-up-and-go of 24.6 s is a falls emergency and is actionable immediately, whereas no further imaging changes management
Education-adjusted norms are necessary to avoid overcalling impairment in a patient with ten years of schooling — and here the deficit survives the adjustment

red_herrings.data_point: Urinary urgency with known prostatic hyperplasia
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attributes the urinary symptom to the prostate and removes it from the neurological syndrome, or conversely completes an NPH triad
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Urinary urgency in severe small-vessel disease is part of the frontal-subcortical syndrome; prostatism coexists, and neither observation supports hydrocephalus in the absence of the imaging phenotype

red_herrings.data_point: Ventricular enlargement with the full clinical triad
red_herrings.intended_effect: Leads to a diagnosis of normal pressure hydrocephalus and to a tap test or shunt referral
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: An Evans index of 0.30 with ventriculomegaly proportionate to parenchymal loss, no disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid space, and a Fazekas 3 burden with eight lacunes is ex vacuo dilatation in severe small-vessel disease

key_educational_points: Severe small-vessel disease reproduces the entire normal pressure hydrocephalus triad; ventricular morphology and gait character make the distinction
Hypertensive damage in other organs supports a vascular attribution when no stroke can be dated
Timed gait testing converts a vague concern about falls into an actionable measurement
Cognitive instruments must be interpreted against education-adjusted norms
